subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core cron-owned rescue watchdog that can restart managed services and run `doctor --repair --non-interactive` once the rebase blockers and real-host proof are addressed?
rationale: The implementation changes core recovery behavior and command/service-control authority; source fixes alone cannot decide whether this automatic repair boundary belongs in core now or should remain external/product-scoped.

options.title: Continue core PR after rebase and proof
options.body: Keep this PR open as the candidate, require the protocol/store/command-cron repairs, and ask for redacted real-host watchdog recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Redirect to the broader recovery issue
options.body: Pause or close this branch and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36314 to settle the desired self-healing architecture before another implementation PR.

options.title: Keep recovery external for now
options.body: Ask contributors to keep watchdog recovery as operator-managed tooling or docs until core exposes a smaller approved API boundary.

recommendation.title: Continue core PR after rebase and proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open as the candidate, require the protocol/store/command-cron repairs, and ask for redacted real-host watchdog recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans daemon/service-control recovery and cron runtime boundaries where this owner has substantial adjacent history.
